task1.title: The life cycle of the salmon
task1.prompt: The diagrams below show the life cycle of a species of large fish called the salmon.

stages.label: Salmon eggs to 'fry'
stages.detail: Salmon eggs are laid among reeds and small stones in the slow-moving upper river, hatching after approx 5-6 months into 'fry' measuring 3-8cm.

stages.label: 'fry' to 'smolt'
stages.detail: The fry travel to the fast-flowing lower river where they stay for approx 4 years and grow into 'smolt' measuring 12-15cm.

stages.label: 'smolt' to 'adult salmon'
stages.detail: The smolt migrate to the open sea, living there for approx 5 years to reach adulthood ('adult salmon', measuring 70-76cm) before swimming back to the upper river.

chartDesc.overview: The life cycle of the salmon is a multi-stage cyclical process taking roughly 9.5 to 10 years, transitioning through three aquatic environments (upper river, lower river, and open sea) and three developmental stages ('fry', 'smolt', and 'adult salmon').
keyFeatures: Cyclical process spanning three locations: upper river (slow moving), lower river (fast flowing), and open sea
Three defined fish stages: (1) 'fry' (3-8cm), (2) 'smolt' (12-15cm), and (3) 'adult salmon' (70-76cm)
Time spent in each location: approx 5-6 months in upper river, approx 4 years in lower river, and approx 5 years in open sea
